stories.headline: Trump administration asks the Supreme Court to let border wall construction resume in Texas’s Big Bend region
stories.summary: The Justice Department on Wednesday asked the Supreme Court to lift a lower-court injunction that has temporarily blocked the Department of Homeland Security from building a border wall and related infrastructure in the Big Bend Sector, which covers more than 500 miles of the U.S.-Mexico border and 77 Texas counties, CBS News reports. “The district court’s injunction significantly frustrates the government’s ability to stop the flow of illegal aliens and drugs across the southern border,” Solicitor General D. John Sauer wrote, saying the project areas were chosen because of high rates of illegal crossings and drug smuggling. The plan calls for 30-foot bollard walls from Fort Quitman to Closed Canyon in Big Bend Ranch State Park, with walls and roads spanning more than 300 miles; construction of a 47-mile stretch began last month and five barrier contracts have been awarded. The project drew bipartisan pushback, along with objections from ranchers and local law enforcement, after bulldozers appeared at Big Bend National Park. CBP says the wall itself won’t cut through the national park, though patrol roads, detection technology and about 17 miles of vehicle barriers would. The administration invoked a 1996 law letting the DHS secretary waive environmental and preservation requirements for border barriers.

stories.headline: Tesla’s Q3: revenue in line at $28 billion, a slight EPS beat, surprise positive cash flow, and Cybercab joins the Austin Robotaxi fleet
stories.summary: Tesla reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $28.05 billion, just under the $28.34 billion expected, and non-GAAP earnings of 48 cents a share, ahead of the 45-cent estimate, Teslarati reports. Operating margin came in at 2.6% on $718 million of operating income, and free cash flow was a positive $1.53 billion against expectations of a large negative number. In its shareholder letter, Tesla said FSD (Supervised) is now attached to more than 75% of new vehicle deliveries in North America, up nearly 20 points from last quarter, and that it has begun volume production of the Tesla Semi, whose top version can go 500 miles fully loaded. Tesla also said it has started deploying Cybercab into its Robotaxi fleet in Austin, where the service has logged nearly two million cumulative unsupervised miles and now runs 6 a.m. to midnight, and that Grok is available in Cybercab. The company plans to reach 400 MW of AI training compute by year-end for vehicle and Optimus autonomy and to begin commissioning equipment at its Austin chip fab in 2027. Net profit still fell sharply from a year ago as spending on AI and Optimus climbed.

stories.headline: U.S. orders non-emergency embassy staff and families out of Saudi Arabia as Houthi attacks on the kingdom escalate
stories.summary: The State Department has ordered non-emergency U.S. government employees and their families to leave Saudi Arabia after a surge in attacks on the kingdom by Iran-backed Houthi militants, CBS News reports. Spokesperson Tommy Pigott said the ordered departure applies “in Saudi Arabia only,” pushing back on a report that it could extend to other Gulf states, though several other embassies have shifted to “restricted operations” staffing. The Houthis have fired drones and missiles at Saudi airports and oil facilities in recent weeks, including an Oct. 10 strike on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport that killed 12 people, one of them an American, and injured more than 300. Saudi air defenses blocked a drone attack on the Shaybah oil field Tuesday, with two people killed by falling debris. The fighting raises fears for shipping through the Bab al-Mandab Strait, which has grown more important as the U.S.-Iran war disrupts the Strait of Hormuz. The U.K. has offered Saudi Arabia defensive air support; it is not clear whether the Trump administration will help, though the president has not ruled out strikes on the Houthis.

stories.headline: No charges for a Michigan woman with a concealed carry permit who shot a man attacking her boyfriend in a Dearborn store
stories.summary: Prosecutors in Wayne County, Michigan, say they will not charge a 30-year-old woman with a concealed carry permit who shot and critically wounded a man attacking her boyfriend inside a Dearborn sneaker store, the Daily Caller reports, citing Detroit station WXYZ. Surveillance video from the White House Kicks store on Saturday appears to show the 36-year-old boyfriend greeting a customer before another man attacks him. “They started fighting, then — lady pulls out her gun and then protects her boyfriend,” a witness said, estimating she fired three or four shots. Dearborn Police Chief Issa Shahin said the men appeared to know each other and that the charging decision belonged to Prosecutor Kym Worthy, adding that charges may yet be filed against the people who started the fight. The wounded man was shot in the back.

stories.headline: Jets get WR Adonai Mitchell and LG Dylan Parham back at practice before the Dolphins game, but Breece Hall still sits
stories.summary: Wide receiver Adonai Mitchell and left guard Dylan Parham returned to practice on a limited basis Wednesday as the Jets began preparing for Sunday’s home AFC East matchup with Miami, the team reports. Mitchell has missed four games after injuring his finger before Week 3 and having a hand procedure; if he plays, the Jets would have their full set of pass catchers for the first time since their season-opening win in Nashville. Parham, who started the first three games, hurt his knee in the loss at Detroit, and Jordan Meredith has started in his place since. Running back Breece Hall (quad) did not practice, though coach Aaron Glenn said, “I love his progression.” Braelon Allen has filled in well, with 220 scrimmage yards over the last two games, ninth-most in the league. Glenn said edge Joseph Ossai (ankle) and linebacker Kiko Mauigoa (thigh) are week-to-week, while DT T’Vondre Sweat and edge Will McDonald IV were limited.

stories.headline: A reviewer’s machine folded the iPhone Duo more than 32,000 times, and the hinge came out feeling the same, even a bit stiffer
stories.summary: Apple hasn’t published hinge-durability numbers for the iPhone Duo the way Samsung does, so tech reviewer Joanna Stern built a custom machine that folded her review unit more than 32,000 times over four nights, MacRumors reports. Stern said the hinge sometimes seemed to be loosening as the count went up, but a calibrated push-pull gauge showed it was actually slightly stiffer afterward. “After 32,000 folds, it felt pretty much the same as day one, which is pretty darn impressive,” she said. She didn’t say whether the crease became more visible, and the test was done with a case on and without fully closing the phone each time. For comparison, Samsung Display says the Galaxy Z Fold7’s screen passed a 500,000-fold test in 2025. MacRumors expects more unofficial stress tests ahead of the Duo’s release.

stories.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Duet, a proactive AI agent that checks your apps, briefs you each morning and does tasks on its own
stories.summary: Anthropic on Wednesday introduced Claude Duet, a proactive AI agent meant to rival Meta’s Muse and OpenAI’s Dots, MacRumors reports. Duet connects to a user’s apps, sends a short brief each morning on important items, checks in every few hours, and alerts the user when something needs attention. It runs in the cloud on its own virtual machine with a browser, so it can finish tasks without access to the user’s computer, from simple admin chores to building web apps. Anthropic says it will ask for approval before sending a message, making a payment, signing a document or deleting a file, and that it does not see passwords or logins for connected accounts. Built on Opus 5.5, Duet uses the memory, skills and connected apps already in a Claude account and keeps everything in one ongoing thread. It is a research preview by waitlist for Pro and Max subscribers in the U.S., on the web and in a standalone iOS app, and counts against existing plan limits.

stories.headline: Sharon Osbourne says she never told Black Sabbath that doctors warned the farewell show could kill Ozzy
stories.summary: Sharon Osbourne says she kept doctors’ warnings about Ozzy Osbourne’s health from Tony Iommi, Geezer Butler and Bill Ward ahead of Black Sabbath’s Back To The Beginning farewell show, Louder reports. Speaking at a London screening of the upcoming documentary Monday night, she said, “The guys didn’t know how sick Ozzy was. Nobody knew,” adding that even their children weren’t told. She had earlier told Rolling Stone that doctors in England strongly advised against the July 5, 2025, show at Villa Park in Birmingham, saying it could kill him, but that Ozzy insisted: “I know I’m dying… This is what I want.” The show near his childhood home in Aston featured Metallica, Slayer, Guns N’ Roses, Tool, Anthrax and others and raised money for local charities. Sharon said Ozzy was “flying high” afterward, “laughing, telling jokes again,” until the day he died. Ozzy & Black Sabbath: Back To The Beginning opens in cinemas worldwide Oct. 28.

stories.headline: Fairfield police recover every dollar of $7,000 a resident handed over in a fake-arrest bail scam
stories.summary: Fairfield police have recovered $7,000 stolen from a resident who was tricked into believing her son had been arrested after a car accident and needed bail money, Patch reports. A caller posing as her son and a second caller pretending to be an attorney told her to withdraw cash and arrange a pickup, and she handed the money to a driver. Officers tracked down the driver, who turned out to be a rideshare driver hired without knowing about the scam, and returned the full amount. “Recovering money lost to financial scams is uncommon,” the department said, urging residents to report fraud quickly. Police reminded residents that they never send messengers to collect bail or take bail payments by phone or credit card, and that anyone who gets a call saying a relative has been arrested should check by calling the police department at an independently found number.

stories.headline: Armed federal agents are knocking on doors in several states to track down possible noncitizen voters before the midterms
stories.summary: Armed, uniformed Homeland Security Investigations agents have been knocking on doors in several states to ask residents about their immigration status and whether they have registered to vote or voted in past elections, a CBS News investigation found. The visits ramped up in September and continued over the past weekend as part of a push to root out noncitizen voters before the midterms. DHS has said as many as 250,000 people could be illegally registered, a figure election experts dispute; the Justice Department says 156 people have been charged with voting-fraud offenses since the start of the Trump administration, out of 227 million registered voters. On Monday the Justice Department announced that HSI agents in California had arrested more than 20 green card holders accused of illegally registering or voting, including a 72-year-old man from Belize accused of voting in the past four elections. “HSI is actively rooting out and investigating election fraud wherever it can be found,” a DHS spokesperson said, adding that only American citizens should be electing American leaders. Protect Democracy, a left-leaning group suing over the campaign, says the armed visits could scare lawful voters.

stories.headline: Sources say it was Elon Musk’s decision that throttled Ukraine’s access to SpaceX’s Starshield network, not an order from Trump or the Pentagon
stories.summary: A decision by Elon Musk led to last week’s restrictions on Ukraine’s use of SpaceX’s Starshield satellite network, people familiar with the matter told CBS News. Musk held several conversations with administration officials beforehand, wanting clarity on President Trump’s thinking, and has expressed distaste for his company being seen as profiting from the war. Last week Musk wrote on X that “any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS,” but the restrictions surprised some officials, who said neither Trump nor the Pentagon ordered limits meant to disrupt drone operations. Trump said Monday he was seeking details on who ordered the slowdown, and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said Tuesday, “We haven’t pulled anything back,” adding that Starlink has the option to make those decisions under its terms of service. Starshield, the military-grade version of Starlink that the U.S. government pays for, normally has no speed cap, but Ukrainian units reported link drops at speeds as low as 90 km/h, grounding the long-range strike drones that cruise at 160 km/h or more. Zelenskyy’s office said Wednesday the service was still throttled. Musk did not respond to a request for comment.

stories.headline: Judge orders Meta to pay New Mexico $25 billion, its biggest fine ever, for deceiving Facebook users about privacy in the Cambridge Analytica scandal
stories.summary: A New Mexico judge on Wednesday ordered Meta to pay the state $25 billion after a jury found the company liable for deceiving users about privacy, the largest penalty ever against Facebook’s owner, PBS NewsHour reports. Jurors in September found Meta committed more than 43 million violations of state consumer protection laws when the political consulting firm Cambridge Analytica harvested Facebook user data to target political ads in the 2016 election. “Facebook promised users that they (the users) controlled their data. This was false,” Judge Francis J. Matthew wrote. The state had sought $35 billion to $40 billion; Meta argued for no more than $3.4 billion and has said it will appeal. Attorney General Raúl Torrez called the ruling “an unambiguous message, to Silicon Valley,” noting that under the state constitution the money goes to education: “We may have paid for the construction of schools for the next 100 years.” The fine dwarfs the $5 billion the FTC imposed in 2019. Meta shares were up about 2% ahead of its quarterly earnings report Wednesday afternoon.

stories.headline: Pope Leo XIV will not need any further treatment after his lung cancer surgery, his doctors say
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV will not need further treatment after surgery for lung cancer, his doctors said Wednesday in an update released by the Vatican press office, NBC News reports. Final analysis of the tissue removed during the operation confirmed “a pulmonary adenocarcinoma and that the disease was localized,” Dr. Luigi Carbone and Prof. Stefano Margaritora said, and “a subsequent oncological evaluation has confirmed that no further therapy is required.” The 71-year-old pope had surgery earlier this month at Rome’s Gemelli Hospital to remove a nodule found during routine tests at what he called “a very early stage.” He was discharged Saturday and returned to public duties Sunday with a prayer from the papal apartment window. “This experience has made me feel particularly close to all those who are experiencing illness and a condition of frailty,” he said, adding that he would “gradually resume my activities, always with God’s help and your prayers.”

stories.headline: A Florida police officer who found a man dead on a welfare check allegedly moved into his house, renovated it and posed as him for years
stories.summary: A Lauderhill, Florida, police officer who helped find a 71-year-old man dead in his home during a 2022 welfare check allegedly moved into the house weeks later and spent years impersonating him, NBC News reports. Brian Louis Sguros, 35, was arrested Tuesday on felony charges including official misconduct and criminal use of a deceased person’s identification. The Broward Sheriff’s Office says Dennis West died of natural causes in July 2022, and that Sguros took possession of the home that August, told the medical examiner’s office he was West’s friend, though there is no sign he knew him, and falsely said West had no living family. Investigators say Sguros paid taxes and utilities in West’s name, used law enforcement databases to look up information about him, and forged West’s signature to get a city permit for repairs. He was ordered held on $25,000 bond Wednesday and has been placed on unpaid administrative leave.

stories.headline: Titans cut defensive lineman Jordan Elliott for bringing a gun to the team facility, but Robert Saleh tells other teams to call him
stories.summary: The Tennessee Titans released defensive lineman Jordan Elliott on Wednesday after he brought a gun to the team’s Nashville training facility on Oct. 15, NBC News reports. Coach Robert Saleh called it “a terrible lapse in judgment that I recognize as a call for help more than a criminal act” and said Elliott is “a good man” who deserves another chance, just not in Tennessee. “Unfortunately rules are rules with regards to guns on (team) property,” Saleh said, adding a message to the league’s other 31 teams: if they need “a hell of a run-stopping D tackle” for a playoff run, “give me a call.” The NFL said its policy bars firearms at team facilities, stadiums, hotels, planes and buses and that the matter is under review. Nashville police were not called. Elliott, in his seventh season after stints with Cleveland and San Francisco, played in Tennessee’s first five games before being listed inactive Sunday for personal reasons.

stories.headline: Westport police charge a New York man with kidnapping after he allegedly beat an ex in his car, crashed near I-95 and tried to run them over
stories.summary: Westport police have charged a Port Chester, New York, man with first-degree kidnapping and attempted first-degree assault after an Oct. 15 incident in which he allegedly assaulted a former partner and tried to run them over, Patch reports. Police say the victim had recently ended the relationship with Vanderval Ferreira, who then made repeated calls and sent texts that included “threats to kill the victim.” The victim agreed to meet him and got into his car; police say he drove erratically around Westport and struck and restrained the victim when they tried to get out. The car hit a guardrail and spun out while entering I-95 at Exit 17, letting the victim escape, and Ferreira allegedly then drove at them as they ran. Ferreira, already jailed on an unrelated matter, was served the warrant Tuesday at Stamford Superior Court, is held on $500,000 bail and is due back in court Dec. 15.

stories.headline: LEGO and Daft Punk tease a mystery collaboration, with clues pointing to a reveal as soon as Thursday
stories.summary: The LEGO Group and Daft Punk have teased an upcoming collaboration, Brick Fanatics reports. The hint came in the electronic duo’s latest WDPK RADIO LIVE YouTube broadcast: about a minute in, a room full of computers shows a box marked “Confidential,” and one of Daft Punk’s metallic gloved hands flips a switch that lights up a red LEGO brick outline with the codes “GM08,” “2007” and “22.10,” the last possibly pointing to a fuller reveal on Oct. 22. No details have been announced. Brick Fanatics speculates it may be tied to “Daft Punk Concert,” a fan-designed LEGO Ideas project by RobotRock that has been awaiting a decision since qualifying for review in 2025. That roughly 2,000-piece build recreates the duo’s Alive 2007 tour stage, with a motorized, lit pyramid of transparent bricks.

stories.headline: Trumbull Health Department holds walk-in flu clinics this week, including Wednesday evening 6–8 p.m. at 335 White Plains Road
stories.summary: The Trumbull Health Department is running walk-in flu clinics this week at 335 White Plains Road, the town announced Tuesday. Sessions are today, Tuesday, Oct. 20, from 10 a.m. to noon and 2 to 4 p.m., and Wednesday, Oct. 21, from 6 to 8 p.m. No appointment is required. The department is offering pediatric nasal and standard flu vaccines for children 3 and older, along with adult and senior doses, while supplies last.

stories.headline: Trumbull’s free Kids Pumpkin Fest is Sunday, Oct. 25 on the Town Hall Green, with touch-a-truck from Long Hill Fire and the Trumbull Police motorcycles
stories.summary: Trumbull Parks & Recreation’s annual Kids Pumpkin Fest returns Sunday, Oct. 25, from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. on the Town Hall Green and gazebo at 5866 Main Street, the town announced Monday. Entry is free and the event runs rain or shine. Planned activities include pumpkin decorating, lawn games, face painting, crafts with the Trumbull Nature & Arts Center, a Long Hill Fire Department touch-a-truck, a Trumbull Police motorcycle encounter, a photo booth by Kait Snook Art & Design, a live DJ, and pastries and coffee from the Brewberry Café truck. Pumpkins and craft supplies are available while they last. Details are on the town’s Kids Pumpkin Fest page.

stories.headline: Trumbull this week: a hearing on a one-year data center moratorium, early voting opens Monday at the library, and a Town Hall Halloween parade
stories.summary: Trumbull’s Planning and Zoning Commission will hold a public hearing Wednesday on a proposed text amendment that would define data centers as their own principal use in the town’s zoning rules and put a one-year moratorium on them, according to the meeting agenda, Patch reports in its weekly look at what’s coming up in town. Early voting for the Nov. 3 election runs Monday, Oct. 19, through Sunday, Nov. 1, at the Trumbull Library, from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., with longer 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. hours on Oct. 27 and Oct. 29, according to the town clerk. Patch also points to First Selectman Vicki Tesoro’s statement on the proposed high-density housing development at 1, 7 and 15 Main St. in Monroe, near the Coventry Lane area of Trumbull; no application is pending in Trumbull, and residents can send comments to the Monroe Planning and Zoning Commission. The Commission on Aging will hear an update on fraud prevention and a Senior Center report, and preschoolers can trick-or-treat through Town Hall in the annual Halloween parade, which has two sessions of 20 children each and requires registration.
